questionReview.question: The gender pay gap can be attributed to differences in economic value between men and women instead of different social expectations.
questionReview.disposition: Retain as disclosed most-likely interpretation; inspect rationale and contextual sources, not a claim of a documented national position.
questionReview.rationale: Educated assumption: Disagree is the most likely institutional interpretation of this specific proposition. The SEA-PLM research covering the Philippines associates learning outcomes with early education and socioeconomic background. These observations give contextual support for experience-sensitive policy; they do not document a state theory of racial or inherited differences. Equality and social-development policy favour disagreement with reducing pay differences to economic value alone. Economic value is not silently equated with biological inheritance. The contextual balance favours this direction over the opposite response, while qualifications make a weak response more appropriate than a strong one. The sources do not document an official answer to this exact statement; the normative comparison and its stated trade-off remain uncertain.
